content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes an Inter-Stage Prompt-Matched Framework for prompt tuning which is applicable for both CNN and Transformer architectures. Pretrained backbones are fixed and divided into stages. The core design is a Semantic-aware Prompt Matcher which transforms the output of the previous stage into the next stage through progressively learning "reasonable prompts" with a recurrent mechanism guided by interim semantic maps.  Experiments on five semantic segmentation benchmarks have been conducted to verify the efffectiveness.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. This paper is easy to follow and the proposed method is technically sound.
2. The proposed method can be applied to both CNNs and Transformers. Experiments on semantic segmentation have verified the effectiveness.

Weakness:
1. The improvement brought by recurrent iterations of SPM is not significant. When pre-trained on COCO, more recurrent iterations even degrade the performance.
2. It seems to me that the proposed SPM is more like an adaptor rather than prompt tuning. Since SPM only transforms the output feature from one stage to the next stage of the pre-trained backbones and there is no real prompt generated or fed into the network, it is not appropriate to treat this method as prompt-tuning approaches. Besides, I also don't understand why the proposed module is named Inter-Stage Prompt Matcher? Which part of the module is doing prompt matching. More explanations is required.
3. The ablation study to verify SPM in Table 6 may be unfair since the compared variants have different model sizes. It is not sure whether the improvement are brought by the architecture design or pure additional model parameters/capacities.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. The proposed method is overall clearly presented. However, the authors should explain what exactly is promt-matching and why the proposed method is for promt-tuning.

2. Table 9 seems to be left undiscussed.

3. Although the proposed framework may be new, I find the overall novelty is not that significant. The idea ot transfer pre-trained network for dense prediction through model adaptor has been explored. One missing reference is as follows and I suggest the authors to include this related work for discussion and comparison:

Chen et al., Vision Transformer Adapter for Dense Predictions, arXiv 2022
content.summary_of_the_review: I think the overall quality of this paper meets the stardard of ICLR. The proposed method is technically sound and most of the techniques have been empirically verified to be effectiveness. My major concern is that the concept of promt-matching is not clearly explained which seems to be the central claim of this paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper focused on fine tuning large pre-trained visual backbone with a small amount of parameters for semantic segmentation.  The key idea in this paper is learning visual prompts in the different stages of a visual backbone while freezing rest of parameters.  Compared with existing visual prompts fine tuning work, this paper presents a new SPM module for learning better representation. Specifically, SPM is implemented as a recurrent network for input features and semantic map,  then the semantic map and input feature will be iteratively update with latent visual prompt feature.  Experiments on 4 datasets consistently shown that the proposed fine tuning method is much better than head fine tuning and close to entire backbone fine tuning.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The key contribution in this paper is the semantic prompts matcher for network fine tuning. Unlike existing method directly inserting visual prompts into backbone layers, the proposed method generating visual prompts from features in different stage and given learned semantic maps. Especially, the designed the recurrent  process allowing the semantic map and visual prompt to be update in SPM internally. 


While the main concerns for this paper is it incremental improvement over existing visual prompt based network fine tuning approaches. Compared to existing methods,  applying semantic map as one of input for visual prompt generation seems to be straightforward.  Also the results on different dataset with marginal improvements (given table 10).
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is well written and the most of technical parts is clear. 

Here are some questions need to be cleared:
1. How M_0 is initialized ?
2. Any results on COCO or cityscape for further evaluation?
content.summary_of_the_review: Since the improvement over existing method is quite limit, it needs more judgement for the proposed method. For example, whether the proposed method can be extended to other applications as M_0 may be replaced by class label or other  semantic map (key points, depth map?)  If there are more justifications for the potential application of the paper, it may help improve the technical contribution.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a new fine-tuning scheme with task-relevant visual prompt learning. By partitioning the backbone network into multiple stages, such scheme can be adopted for various CNNs and Transformers. And a lightweight Semantic-aware Prompt Matcher (SPM) is developed to learn reasonable prompts with a recurrent mechanism.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: This paper is well written, and contributes a task-relevant visual prompt learning scheme for pre-trained backbone with frozen parameters, which enables avoid the modification of foundation units in backbone network and learn reasonable task-relevant visual prompts incorporated with interim semantic maps. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves a promising performance.
Weakness:
I have several concerns.
1.	This paper finds that interim semantic maps generated at intermediate layers can provide fine-grained prior information. However, this paper does not provide theoretical analysis and visual results to explain the role of interim semantic maps.
2.	This paper does not evaluate the quality of the produced features. Please provide the compared visualization results and analysis with other baseline methods. 
3.	Please provide the analysis on the fine-tuning time and inference latency.
4.	The performance of backbone network is not presented in Table 6,7,8,9.
5.	How to ensure the loss weight of the interim semantic maps generated by SPM?

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces Inter-Stage Prompt-Matched Framework for generic and effective visual prompt tuning. In particular, a frozen backbone with different stages is jointly finetuned with learnable prompt to refine the mask results. Extensive experiments on five benchmarks show that the proposed scheme can achieve a promising trade-off between parameter efficiency and performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength 
1, The motivation is clear and easy to follow.

2, Results on ADE-20k and Vaihingen show the effectiveness of proposed approaches over different baseline.


Weakness.

1. Novelty

1.1, The bottom-up refined architecture of Inter-Stage Prompt-Matched Framework is common in previous works for semantic segmentation. Besides, this work does not show the performance advantage over previous method.

AlignSeg: Feature-Aligned Segmentation Networks-PAMI-2021

1.2, The Semantic-aware Prompt Matcher itself is also not novel. Several previous works proposed the similar idea to consider the multi-stage context for semantic segmentation. Here are some examples.

Semantic Correlation Promoted Shape-Variant Context for Segmentation CVPR-2019
Semantic Flow for Fast and Accurate Scene Parsing  ECCV-2020

2. Results:

2.1, Not very significant improvements over baseline in Tab.1 and Tab.2.

2.2, What about the stronger setting? For example, using stronger backbone and show more significant improvements. 

2.3. What about comparing with STOA methods? 

3. Presentation:The presentation is not good and make it hard to follow. Here are several examples: 

3.1, “The objective of this work is to explore how to effectively and efficiently adapt pretrained visual foundation models to downstream tasks, e.g., image semantic segmentation” where are other downstream tasks?

3.2, In the first part of introduction, the author did not cite any related works on fine-tuning or prompt-tuning.

3.3, Where does M_{0} come from?

3.4,  Does the Pyramid Dilation Convolution is the only choice for your framework?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Clarity is good. Quality and Novelty are not. No reference code is provided, but the details are enough.
content.summary_of_the_review: Based on strength and weakness, I choose to reject this paper mainly due to the novelty and performance.

content.title: Prompt-Matched Semantic Segmentation
content.abstract: The objective of this work is to explore how to effectively and efficiently adapt pre-trained visual foundation models to downstream tasks, e.g., image semantic segmentation. Conventional methods usually fine-tuned the entire networks for each specific dataset, which will be burdensome to store massive parameters of these networks. Several recent works attempted to insert some extra trainable parameters into the frozen networks to learn visual prompts for parameter-efficient tuning. However, these works showed poor generality as they were designed specifically for Transformers. Moreover, using limited information in these schemes, they exhibited a poor capacity to learn effective prompts. To alleviate these issues, we propose a novel Inter-Stage Prompt-Matched Framework for generic and effective visual prompt tuning. Specifically, to ensure generality, we divide the pre-trained backbone with frozen parameters into multiple stages and perform prompt learning between different stages, which makes the proposed scheme applicable to various architectures of CNN and Transformer. For effective tuning, a lightweight Semantic-aware Prompt Matcher (SPM) is designed to progressively learn reasonable prompts with a recurrent mechanism, guided by the rich information of interim semantic maps. Working as a deep matched filter of representation learning, the proposed SPM can well transform the output of the previous stage into a desirable input for the next stage, thus achieving the better matching/stimulating for the pre-trained knowledge. Finally, we apply the proposed method to handle various semantic segmentation tasks. Extensive experiments on five benchmarks show that the proposed scheme can achieve a promising trade-off between parameter efficiency and performance effectiveness.
